name: Judiciary

levels.note: 12th pass + typing. Age 18-27. Computer certificate preferred.
LLB degree. Age 21-35. PCS(J) exam by state PSC.
LLM or 7 years practice. Age 35-45. Higher Judicial Service exam.

stages.name: Preliminary Exam
stages.tests: 100-150 Qs — Law (Civil/Criminal/Constitutional), GK, English. Objective type.
stages.note: Qualifying. Cut-off varies by state and category.

stages.name: Main Exam (Written)
stages.tests: 3-4 papers: Civil Law, Criminal Law, English, Language (Hindi/Regional). Descriptive.
stages.note: Merit prepared from Main score. 3 hrs per paper.

stages.name: Interview
stages.tests: 20-30 min panel. Legal knowledge, personality, aptitude for judicial service.

stages.name: Training & Posting
stages.tests: 6-12 months judicial training at state judicial academy.
stages.note: Posted as Civil Judge / Judicial Magistrate after training.

reality: Judicial service exams are state-specific. Each state has its own syllabus and pattern.
PCS(J) is one of the most competitive exams. 10,000+ applicants for 100-200 vacancies.
Law degree (LLB) is mandatory. 3-year or 5-year LLB both accepted.
Some states require 2-3 years of practice for HJS (Higher Judicial Service).
Judges have job security but heavy workload. 50-100 cases per day in trial courts.
Salary: Civil Judge ~₹77,840 (Level 10) + DA + HRA. District Judge ~₹1,44,840 (Level 12).

syllabus.pattern: Objective paper on substantive and procedural law plus general knowledge, with negative marking in most states. Marks, sections and the number of questions are fixed by each High Court's notification.

topics.items: Code of Civil Procedure, Indian Contract Act, Transfer of Property Act, Specific Relief Act, Limitation Act, Hindu Marriage Act, Indian Succession Act
Indian Penal Code / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Code of Criminal Procedure / Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, Indian Evidence Act / Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam
Constitution of India, torts, consumer protection, family law, local rent and land laws of the state

syllabus.books: PCS(J) Guide (Amazon) · Flipkart

syllabus.pattern: Written papers in civil law, criminal law, English (essay and precis) and the state language or Hindi, with a translation paper. Several states add judgment writing. Each High Court sets its own paper structure and marks.

topics.items: Problem-based questions that require applying sections and citing case law, not reciting definitions
Essay, precis, comprehension and translation — qualifying in some states but counted in others
Framing issues, marshalling facts, applying law and writing a reasoned order

syllabus.books: Judicial Services Mains Guide (Amazon)

syllabus.pattern: Oral examination on law, procedure and the candidate's background, conducted by the High Court's selection committee after the mains.

topics.items: Leading cases, procedural steps, recent amendments, legal current affairs, and the candidate's practice or academic specialisation

syllabus.exam: Bare Acts and case law — the real syllabus
syllabus.pattern: Judicial service exams are set from bare Acts and leading judgments. State notifications list the exact statutes, and the list differs between states.

topics.items: Read the bare Act section by section and annotate it with leading cases; do not rely on guides alone, because the papers quote sections directly
Constitutional law and procedural law judgments of the Supreme Court; recent amendments to criminal law

faq.q: What is PCS(J) and how is it different from UPSC?
faq.a: PCS(J) = Provincial Civil Service (Judicial). State-level exam for Civil Judge posts. UPSC conducts exams for central services (IAS, IPS). Different eligibility, syllabus, and recruiting body.

faq.q: Can a 3-year LLB graduate apply for judicial service?
faq.a: Yes. 3-year LLB after graduation or 5-year integrated LLB both accepted. Some states require minimum age 21-22 and maximum 35.

faq.q: Is practice experience required for judicial service?
faq.a: For lower judiciary (Civil Judge): no experience required in most states. For higher judiciary (District Judge): 7 years practice required. Check state-specific rules.

faq.q: What is the age limit for judicial service exams?
faq.a: Civil Judge: 21-35 years (varies by state). District Judge: 35-45 years. Age relaxations for SC/ST/OBC/PwD.

faq.q: How many vacancies are there in judiciary?
faq.a: UP: 100-200 (Civil Judge) annually. Bihar: 100-150. Total judicial vacancies exceed 2000 per year across India. High Courts recruit separately.

faq.q: Where do I find official judiciary notifications?
faq.a: State PSC websites (uppsc.up.nic.in, bpsc.bihar.gov.in) and High Court websites. SarkariJobs+ links the official notification on every listing.

prepPlan.what: Read CPC, CrPC/BNSS, IPC/BNS, Evidence Act/BSA and the Constitution from the bare Act, section by section, annotating leading cases. Guides summarise; the papers quote sections.
Add the state rent control, land revenue and local laws named in your High Court's notification. This is where candidates who studied only central law lose marks.
Judicial mains is problem-based. Write answers applying the section to the facts, then cite one or two cases. Practise judgment writing and the essay paper weekly.
Solve previous papers of your state and two neighbouring states. Prelims repeats sections and case names; track every wrong answer by statute.
Revise annotated bare Acts and your case list. Prepare for the viva: recent Supreme Court judgments, amendments and your own academic or practice background.
